```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

studies <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "text_study_level.csv"),
                    show_col_types = FALSE)
counts <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "text_in_text_numbers.csv"),
                   show_col_types = FALSE)
f3_pooled <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "figure_3_meta_summary.csv"),
                      show_col_types = FALSE)

share_positive <- mean(studies$estimate > 0)
n_positive <- sum(studies$estimate > 0)
n_negative <- sum(studies$estimate < 0)
n_zero <- sum(studies$estimate == 0)
n_resp_gender <- f3_pooled$n_studies[f3_pooled$resp_female == "Female respondents"]

# Any significance rule is a threshold on the ratio of an estimate to its standard error,
# and both counts rise as that threshold is relaxed. Tightening it until only 23 positive
# estimates survive, and loosening it until 11 negative ones do, brackets what any rule can
# reach.
z <- abs(studies$estimate / studies$std.error)
threshold_23_positive <- sort(z[studies$estimate > 0], decreasing = TRUE)[23]
negatives_there <- sum(studies$estimate < 0 & z >= threshold_23_positive)
threshold_11_negative <- sort(z[studies$estimate < 0], decreasing = TRUE)[11]
positives_there <- sum(studies$estimate > 0 & z >= threshold_11_negative)

appendix_cells <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "figure_a2_a45_plotted_estimates.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE)
n_costa <- sum(appendix_cells$figure_number == 18)
n_appendix_cells <- 2 * sum(appendix_cells$figure_number != 18)

# The prose spells small counts out, so the spine's row count has to be spelled too.
spelled <- function(n) {
  words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten")
  if (n <= length(words)) words[n] else as.character(n)
}
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and the document below is rendered
# from it. The same rows are written out as errata_entries.csv at the foot of this file, so
# any other rendering of these corrections (the README's counts, a remastered edition) reads
# them rather than keeping a second hand-typed copy that can drift out of agreement.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes, and is the only markup a field carries. Each renderer
# resolves it its own way: bold here, \was{} in an edition. Everything else in a field is
# literal text.
#
# Numbering is the published note's and is APPEND-ONLY: an entry number may already have been
# cited, so a later finding is added at the end and never interleaved, merged or split.
#
# Entry 1 corrects the same overstatement in two places, so its published and corrected
# fields each hold two passages joined by a blank line, and its location holds both pages
# joined by "; ". Its emitter splits them back apart. It is one error and stays one row.
#
# `form` is a renderer's choice of treatment: "full" where the published and corrected
# fields are whole sentences that need setting as blocks, "brief" where the entry is a token
# replacement.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note,

  1, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The share of studies with a positive effect is overstated, in two places",
  "published p. 659; published p. 664",
  paste(
    "Across the 67 studies we summarize, [[three-fourths]] find a positive effect of being described as a woman.",
    "We observe considerable study-to-study variation, although [[more than three-fourths]] of the studies show a positive effect.",
    sep = "\n\n"),
  str_glue(
    "Across the 67 studies we summarize, [[{sprintf('%.0f%%', 100 * share_positive)}]] find a positive effect of being described as a woman.",
    "\n\n",
    "We observe considerable study-to-study variation, although [[{sprintf('%.0f%%', 100 * share_positive)}]] of the studies show a positive effect."),
  str_glue(
    "Of the 67 study-level estimates, {n_positive} are positive, {n_negative} are negative ",
    "and {n_zero} is exactly zero. The positive share is ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', 100 * share_positive)} per cent, which is below three-fourths rather ",
    "than above it. The claim the two sentences make is unaffected: positive effects are the ",
    "large majority."),

  2, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The count of negative estimates omits two studies",
  "published p. 662",
  "We see a very consistent pattern in favor of women candidates on average: 47 estimates are positive (23 significant) and [[18]] are negative (11 significant).",
  str_glue("We see a very consistent pattern in favor of women candidates on average: 47 estimates are positive (23 significant) and [[{n_negative}]] are negative (11 significant)."),
  str_glue(
    "The deposited estimates divide into {n_positive} positive, {n_negative} negative and ",
    "{n_zero} exactly zero, which is the only division summing to 67. The published 47 plus ",
    "18 sums to 65.",
    "\n\n",
    "The two parenthetical counts of significant estimates are left as published, because no ",
    "corrected value for them can be stated. They correspond to no significance rule the ",
    "deposited estimates support, and not merely to a rule with a different threshold: both ",
    "counts rise as a threshold is relaxed, so no threshold can produce 23 and 11 at once. ",
    "Tightening the threshold until only 23 positive estimates remain significant leaves ",
    "{negatives_there} negative ones; loosening it until 11 negative estimates are ",
    "significant leaves {positives_there} positive ones. The confidence interval rule the ",
    "deposited script itself applies gives {counts$n_pos_sig_ci} and {counts$n_neg_sig_ci}, ",
    "and a test of p below 0.05 gives {counts$n_pos_sig_p05} and {counts$n_neg_sig_p05} and ",
    "cannot be what was done in any case, because {counts$n_missing_p} of the 67 studies ",
    "carry no p-value. The repository records this as unresolved rather than corrected."),

  3, "float", "pipeline", "full",
  "Appendix Figure A.18 prints none of its estimates",
  "",
  str_glue(
    "Figure A.18, Costa (2020), USA - Lucid, is the one study in the appendix whose ",
    "randomized attribute levels are whole tweets. At the width the appendix uses, those row ",
    "labels push the plotting panel, the points, the confidence intervals, the estimate ",
    "labels and the horizontal axis off the right edge of the page. What is printed is a ",
    "column of truncated sentences, an axis title cut off after four letters, and [[no ",
    "data]]. None of the {n_costa} conditional effects the figure is drawn from appears on ",
    "the page."),
  paste(
    "Nothing is wrong with the estimates themselves; they are in the deposited archive and",
    "are unchanged. [[The figure as it should have appeared]]:"),
  "",

  4, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  str_glue("Figure 3 covers {n_resp_gender} experiments, not 36"),
  "published p. 663",
  "Figure 3 shows the CATEs of candidate gender, conditional on respondent gender, for the [[36]] experiments where we were able to identify respondent gender.",
  str_glue("Figure 3 shows the CATEs of candidate gender, conditional on respondent gender, for the [[{n_resp_gender}]] experiments where we were able to identify respondent gender."),
  str_glue(
    "The deposited respondent-gender file carries {n_resp_gender} studies, and the published ",
    "figure itself draws {n_resp_gender} rows in each of its two panels. Figure 3 is correct ",
    "as printed and is not reproduced here; only the sentence describing it miscounts. ",
    "Nothing plotted is affected and neither pooled estimate moves."),

  5, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "The Clayton and Nyhan (2020) manuscript has six authors",
  "published p. 666",
  paste(
    "[[Clayton, Katherine, and Brendan Nyhan]]. 2020. \"Who Will Defend Democracy? ",
    "Evaluating Tradeoffs in Candidate Support among Partisan Donors and Voters.\" ",
    "Unpublished manuscript."),
  paste(
    "Carey, John, Katherine Clayton, Gretchen Helmke, Brendan Nyhan, Mitchell Sanders, and ",
    "Susan Stokes. 2020. \"Who Will Defend Democracy? Evaluating Tradeoffs in Candidate ",
    "Support among Partisan Donors and Voters.\" Unpublished manuscript."),
  paste(
    "The manuscript at the URL the entry itself prints carries six authors on its title",
    "page, in the alphabetical order given above. Crossref, doi 10.33774/apsa-2019-wjva3-v4:",
    "Nyhan, Helmke, Sanders, Clayton, Carey, Stokes, and the same six on every posted",
    "version of the preprint. The short form is therefore Carey et al. (2020), which the",
    "article uses as a study label in six further places: two rows of Table 1, two rows of",
    "the appendix's study table, and the titles of appendix Figures A.16 and A.17. The",
    "appendix's own reference list carries the same two-author entry. Only the labels change:",
    "no estimate, standard error, sample size or study is affected, and neither of the two",
    "experiments the label names is misidentified.")
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note), as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document. Another renderer resolves it differently.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")
plain <- function(x) str_remove_all(x, "\\[\\[|\\]\\]")
```

This note lists `r spelled(nrow(entries))` errors in "What Have We Learned about Gender from Candidate Choice Experiments? A Meta-Analysis of Sixty-Seven Factorial Survey Experiments," published in *The Journal of Politics* 84(2), doi [10.1086/716290](https://doi.org/10.1086/716290). **None of them changes a conclusion of the paper.** They are recorded because the published record is wrong and a reader who quoted it would be misled.

Every corrected value in entries 1 to `r max(entries$entry[entries$class != "bibliographic"])` is computed from the deposited replication archive ([10.7910/DVN/R27ULT](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/R27ULT)) at the time this document is rendered. Entry `r entries$entry[entries$class == "bibliographic"]` corrects a reference-list entry, which the deposit cannot speak to, and is verified instead against the cited manuscript's own title page and the authoritative record at Crossref. The maintained code is at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/schwarz_coppock_2022](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/schwarz_coppock_2022).

```{r entry-1, results="asis"}
# The one entry that quotes two passages: one row, two pages, two published-corrected pairs.
e <- entries |> filter(entry == 1)
pages <- str_remove(str_split_1(e$location, "; "), "^published ")
published_passages <- str_split_1(e$published, "\n\n")
corrected_passages <- str_split_1(e$corrected, "\n\n")

cat("## 1. ", e$title, "\n\n", sep = "")
walk(seq_along(pages), function(i) {
  cat("Published, ", pages[i], ":\n\n> ", bold(published_passages[i]),
      "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(corrected_passages[i]), "\n\n", sep = "")
})
cat(e$note, "\n", sep = "")
```

```{r entry-2, results="asis"}
e <- entries |> filter(entry == 2)
cat("\n\n## 2. ", e$title, "\n\nPublished, ", str_remove(e$location, "^published "), ":\n\n> ",
    bold(e$published), "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
```

```{r entry-3, results="asis"}
# The corrected artifact is the figure below rather than a sentence, so this entry quotes
# nothing: its two paragraphs describe the defect and what replaces it.
e <- entries |> filter(entry == 3)
cat("\n\n## 3. ", e$title, "\n\n", plain(e$published), "\n\n", plain(e$corrected), "\n", sep = "")
```
